extracted.intended_audience: prospective NDSEG fellowship applicants (U.S. citizens and nationals seeking doctoral study in science & engineering)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate (NDSEG) Fellowship program: goals, eligible disciplines, eligibility, application mechanism, sponsors, and participant benefits for prospective doctoral applicants in military-relevant S&E fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDSEG Fellowship program was established in 1989 by direction of congress as an approach to increasing the number of United States (U.S.) citizens receiving doctoral degrees in science and engineering (S&E) disciplines of military importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to frame the program's selection priorities: emphasis on producing U.S. citizen doctoral graduates in S&E areas that support national defense/military needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility: citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to U.S. citizens and U.S. nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or nationals to compete for NDSEG fellowships (this is a core eligibility requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research areas / disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The broad research area disciplines include, but are not limited to: aeronautical and astronautical engineering, Astrodynamics, biomedical engineering, biosciences (includes toxicology); chemical engineering; chemistry; civil engineering; cognitive, neural, and behavioral sciences; computer and computational sciences; electrical engineering; geosciences (includes terrain, water, and air); materials science and engineering; mathematics; mechanical engineering; naval architecture and ocean engineering (includes undersea systems); oceanography (includes ocean acoustics, remote sensing, and marine meteorology); physics (including optics) and space physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative ('includes, but are not limited to'), indicating flexibility; proposals should align with S&E disciplines of military importance as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application mechanism: DoD Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants compete for Fellowship opportunities listed under DoD’s Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs) in research development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should consult and apply via the DoD BAAs/application portal specified by the NDSEG program; adherence to BAA procedures and timelines is implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection and program scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The highly competitive Fellowship Program has awarded nearly 4700 fellowships from over 70,000 applications to U.S. citizens and nationals since its inception in 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect strong competition; historical acceptance rates indicate selectivity. No specific scoring criteria are listed here, but competitiveness is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellow benefit: choice of U.S. institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected Fellows can choose the U.S. Institution to attend for pursuit of their doctoral degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees are not constrained to a pre-assigned school by the fellowship—this is a notable fellowship perk to consider when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship / program authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDSEG Fellowship is sponsored by the Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR), the Army Research Office (ARO), and the Office of Naval Research (ONR) under the direction of the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research & Engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and proposals should understand the Department of Defense research sponsors and priorities may influence funding emphases and topic relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity / nondiscrimination statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDSEG Program is an equal opportunity program open to all qualified U.S. citizens and U.S. nationals without regard to race, sex (including gender and transgender status), age, religion, national origin, disability, marital status, veteran status, registered domestic partner or civil union status, gender identity, medical condition, genetic information, sexual orientation, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and program administration are represented as nondiscriminatory; applicants should not be excluded on listed protected bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research relevance: military importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The program focuses on S&E disciplines 'of military importance' and applicants are described as 'interested in furthering their education in the disciplines of military importance'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals/applications should demonstrate relevance to military or defense-related S&E research development to align with NDSEG's stated mission.
